title: Thermodynamics · Stretch
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Thermodynamics.

concepts.def: Sum of the random kinetic and potential energies of all particles in a system.
ΔU = Q + W. Energy added as heat plus work done on the system equals the change in internal energy.
The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases; heat flows from hot to cold spontaneously.
A measure of disorder; S = k ln W, where W is the number of microstates.
A device that converts thermal energy into mechanical work using a temperature difference.
Maximum theoretical efficiency of a heat engine: η = 1 − T_cold/T_hot, with temperatures in kelvin.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Thermodynamics — a core area of A-Level Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Thermodynamics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Thermodynamics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which best describes the second law of thermodynamics?
options: Energy is conserved in any process.
The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases.
Heat flows spontaneously from cold to hot.
Work and heat are equivalent forms of energy.

mcqs.q: A heat engine operates between 500 K and 300 K. Its maximum theoretical efficiency is:

free_texts.q: Type the key term that means: "ΔU = Q + W. Energy added as heat plus work done on the system equals the change in internal energy."
free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.
